issues.description: Stock API naming mismatch: the problem statement UML and the reference solution declare a method Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) for adding a StockIngredient to the stock, but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. A student implementing SealSaloon according to the UML (or using the solution as example) will call stock.addToStockIngredients(...) which does not exist in the template, causing a compilation failure and confusion about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Stock API name consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: add a method public void addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient ingredient) to the template Stock class (or rename addItem to addToStockIngredients) so the template matches the UML and solution. If you keep addItem, update the problem statement UML and the solution to use addItem everywhere. Keeping both (implement addToStockIngredients delegating to addItem) is also acceptable to maintain backwards compatibility while matching the specification.
